$comment: Negative half of the env-006/env-007 pair pinning RFC-AITP-0001 §7 directly at the envelope layer, the artifact the section's own text describes. `trace_id` is placed as a SIBLING of the schema-defined top-level members, not inside `extensions` — the case RFC-AITP-0012 does not reserve. `aitp-envelope.schema.json` sets `additionalProperties: false` at the top level, so this is a schema-level rejection. Otherwise byte-identical to env-005's fresh, valid shape, so the unknown field is the only defect under test.
description: Envelope carries one unrecognized top-level member (`trace_id`) beside its known, schema-defined fields — not inside `extensions`. RFC-AITP-0001 §7: unknown JSON fields outside `extensions` MUST be rejected — silently ignoring them would create signature ambiguity across implementations, since the envelope signing input (RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4) is computed over the wire object one peer received and another peer, having dropped the unrecognized field first, would reconstruct different bytes. Receivers MUST reject with UNKNOWN_FIELD. Counterpart: env-007, which places an unrecognized key INSIDE `extensions` and MUST succeed.

expected.rationale: `trace_id` is not a member `aitp-envelope.schema.json` defines and it is not inside `extensions`, so RFC-AITP-0001 §7's MUST-reject applies. The envelope is otherwise fresh, structurally valid, and within the tolerance window; the unknown sibling field is the only defect under test.
